learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire a comprehensive understanding of the practical application and theoretical foundations of the respective seminar topics. The seminar promotes broad and integrated knowledge by encouraging participants to independently access current research literature and engage with the latest developments and technologies.

Through active participation in the seminar and the processing of specific research questions or projects, students develop a critical understanding of the most important theories, principles, and methods in the respective subject area. They are capable of independently expanding their knowledge beyond the study program by exploring specialized aspects of the subject area.

Participants of the seminar critically reflect on and evaluate the validity and applicability of theories and methods in real and hypothetical scenarios. They learn to analyze complex problems from different perspectives and develop epistemologically sound arguments. The seminar places particular emphasis on students learning to critically question and relate technical content to arrive at well-founded, innovative solutions.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental and current issues in computer science
Independent development of a given limited topic area using specialized literature and other sources
Written and oral presentation of the prepared topic
assessment_rules: The graded examination can be a presentation (with written elaboration), a term paper, or a portfolio examination. The portfolio examination comprises 100 points, consisting of four elements: research question/outline (20 points), rough concept (20 points), final elaboration (30 points), and presentation & discussion (30 points). For a presentation with written elaboration, it is 20 minutes with a 10-page elaboration. A term paper is 15 pages. For the portfolio, the research question is 1 page, rough concept 3 pages, project report 10 pages, and presentation 20 minutes.
